'''Michael Norman Royston Ashfold''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] is a British [[chemist]] and  Professor of Physical Chemistry at [[University of Bristol]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bris.ac.uk/chemistry/peoplenav/|title=People navigation &#124; School of Chemistry &#124; University of Bristol|first=University of|last=Bristol|website=bris.ac.uk}}</ref>
He is a 2011 Royal Society Leverhulme Trust Senior Research Fellow.<ref name="Royal Society">{{cite web | title=Michael Ashfold | website=Royal Society | url=https://royalsociety.org/people/michael-ashfold-11010/ | access-date=27 August 2022}}</ref>

He graduated BSc in 1975 and PhD in 1978 from Birmingham University.

His fields of research include ultraviolet [[photochemistry]], optical diagnostic methods implemented on microwave-activated methane/hydrogen plasmas in the context of diamond growth via chemical vapour deposition, diamond [[thin film]] investigations and the study of [[nanostructure]]d thin films.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bris.ac.uk/chemistry/people/mike-n-ashfold/index.html| title = Professor Mike Ashfold| publisher = University of Bristol|accessdate = 19 June 2012}}</ref>

==Awards==
*1989 [[Corday–Morgan Medal]] of the Royal Society of Chemistry
*1996 [[Tilden Prize]] of the Royal Society of Chemistry
*2009 Elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]
